findings.issue: The module-level helper `record(count, lineUp)` (plays a run) shares its name with the `record` (HandRecord) destructured inside expectSameReplays and the SPEC-03 loop, so the same identifier means two different things in one file.
findings.evidence: line 30 `function record(count: number, ...)`; line 46 `const { record } = hand;`; SPEC-03 loop `const { record, final } = hand;`.

summary: All in-scope SPEC items are implemented and tested. Recorded deviations judged on substance and accepted: (1) userPolicy is carried as HandSetup.userPolicy / PlaytestOptions.userPolicy, applied only to seat 1 in playHand, so no locked seam-key or .length test changes; (2) the 1,000-hand SPEC-01/02 runs are TLH_SLOW_TESTS opt-in (added to test:slow) with always-on 100-hand versions that use the same assertions and proportional minimums (>= n/10 user hands, >= n bot actions, every Mixed style >= 1). The first 100 Mixed hands include replaced bots whose style changes (line-up first changes at hand 73), so the always-on run still covers replaced styles through hand.lineUp. SPEC-03 runs on the first 200 hands in which seat 1 decides (the length is asserted) from a 250-hand Mixed run (1,000 when slow). Mutation checks on replayWithBots/playHand/runPlaytest, each restored afterwards: re-applying the recorded bot actions instead of letting bots decide is caught by SPEC-03 (SPEC-01/02 cannot tell by design); bots deciding with another replay code is caught by SPEC-01/02/03 and SPEC-06; ignoring lineUp is caught by SPEC-02/03; ignoring the user script is caught by SPEC-01/02/03 and SPEC-06; runPlaytest dropping userPolicy is caught by the SPEC-04 unit test; applying userPolicy to the wrong seat is caught by SPEC-04 and the acceptance tests. TLH_SLOW_TESTS=1 run: 5/5 pass (11 s + 16 s for the 1,000-hand tests). Default 10,000-hand playtest SHA = 442dbf55...08fbc (unchanged); Mixed run shows 0 violations. Locked test sha matches state.json; no other existing test file was edited. No BLOCKER/MAJOR findings.
